validation.name: recorded calls replay
validation.criterion: each recorded module reproduces its recorded output from its recorded inputs: rel_max <= 1e-6 in-process, <= 1e-5 for saved fixtures replayed on another machine

validation.name: recorder CLI on a saved tiny DiT
validation.criterion: outputs equal a direct forward, rel_max <= 1e-6

fixtures.dit: scenarios av (video+audio, padded text mask, token types; 51 calls of every primitive and block), video_only (blocks), rope_pos (repeated temporal position 0; blocks)
fixtures.dit_variants: 7 fused-block flag combinations (cross_gates, fix_modulation, ca_rope) other than the released all-true one; fused blocks recorded
fixtures.vocoder: mel [1,16,12] -> waveform [1,1,192]; 232 calls (Snake, filters, AMP blocks, transposed convs)
fixtures.piflow: released Lite-distill config, 10 steps for a video-like [1,3,2,3,16] and an audio-like [1,6,40] sample with widened random model outputs

skipped.what: running the recorder on real checkpoints
skipped.reason: out of scope for spec 01; done in later specs

deviations.what: bfloat16 tensors are stored once in their own dtype, not also as float32
deviations.why: bfloat16 -> float32 is exact; load_fixture(backend='numpy') returns the float32 copy

deviations.what: parameters left constant by default init (norm scales/biases, learnable gains, Snake alpha/beta) get deterministic noise; audio VAE data_mean/data_std buffers too
deviations.why: otherwise these parameters would not affect outputs and parity tests could not catch wrong handling of them

deviations.what: replay tolerance 1e-5 for saved fixtures replayed on another machine
deviations.why: the GitHub macOS runner reproduced the video VAE decoder recordings at rel_max 3.3e-6: float32 convolution reductions run in a different order on a different CPU; same-machine and in-process replays meet 1e-6
fixture and recorder tests need PyTorch and diffusers

follow_ups: Fixture byte-identity holds per machine; another CPU may produce float32 differences around 1e-6.
Real-weight recordings (spec 05+) need a machine with the checkpoint, e.g. Kaggle.
A video VAE encoder fixture is added in spec 12.

architecture_notes.note: torch CPU float32 runs of the real audio decode take 7.4 s and of the video VAE a few minutes locally; the Lite DiT in float32 needs about 12.5 GB of RAM plus recordings, which is why its reference runs on Kaggle.
architecture_notes.optimization: Record each real-weight reference once and replay it; never put the torch reference in a timing loop.

architecture_notes.note: Recording every block input at Smoke size would be about 2 GB for the DiT; spec 05 records only the first block's inputs of each chain and every output (about 0.8 GB).
architecture_notes.optimization: Chain block inputs from previous outputs in any future large recording.
